rv.q: Liv Hennessy’s sparky theatre rendition wittily highlights how in court it became a clash of civilisations.
The story is a giddy mix of celebrity and salaciousness, and Hennessy makes a hugely entertaining evening of it.
Lucy May Barker as Vardy, proudly tottering through the scene — all poise and no clue — is a comedic visual marvel.
My feeling is that, yes, it is still fun but there's now a hint of stale buns about the case.
Highly recommended as an amusing, fun piece of theatre, well staged and appealing to the full house which shouted, cheered, groaned and, above all, laughed in the right places.
This adaptation of a well-known cultural phenomenon is an autopsy of the intricacies behind existence as a partner of one of England's highest profile footballers.
Vardy V Rooney The Wagatha Christie Trial is terrifically gripping.
No fiction writer could invent this; it is all so utterly ridiculous that it could only possibly be true.

cn.t: Critics enthusiastically praise this verbatim courtroom drama, celebrating its witty adaptation of trial transcripts and sharp direction that transforms the infamous celebrity libel case into compelling, bitingly funny theatre.
